subject: History
description: Covers Enfield rifle, Nana Saheb, and GOI Act 1858.

questions.stem: The spark that ignited the Revolt of 1857 was the introduction of the new Enfield rifle. What was the specific rumor regarding the cartridges of this rifle that enraged the sepoys?

options.option_text: The cartridges were greased with the fat of cows and pigs
The cartridges were intentionally manufactured with rusted iron to cause injuries
The gunpowder was mixed with crushed bones of sacred animals
The cartridges were inscribed with offensive religious symbols

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The new Enfield P-53 rifle required soldiers to bite off the end of a greased paper cartridge before loading it. A widespread rumor circulated among the sepoys that this grease was made from a mixture of beef fat (offensive to Hindus, who revere the cow) and pork fat (forbidden for Muslims). This convinced the sepoys that the British were intentionally trying to destroy their religions.
DECOY BUSTING: The "crushed bones in flour" was another rumor circulating at the time, but the specific trigger for the mutiny was the greased cartridge.
EXAM INSIGHT: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Native Infantry at Barrackpore was the first to openly mutiny against his officers over this issue on March 29, 1857, leading to his hanging.

questions.stem: During the Revolt of 1857, who led the incredibly fierce and prolonged resistance against the British forces in the city of Kanpur?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Nana Saheb, the adopted son of the exiled Maratha Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the rebellion in Kanpur. The British had refused to grant him his father's pension under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse. He was assisted by his brilliant military commander, Tantia Tope.
DECOY BUSTING: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt in Lucknow (Awadh). Kunwar Singh, an 80-year-old Zamindar, famously led the revolt in Bihar (Arrah). Rani Lakshmibai led the revolt in Jhansi.
EXAM INSIGHT: After the recapture of Kanpur by the British under Sir Colin Campbell, Nana Saheb escaped to Nepal and was never captured or heard from again.

questions.stem: The Revolt of 1857 fundamentally changed the administration of India. Which historic document officially transferred the power to govern India from the East India Company directly to the British Crown?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Following the shock of the mutiny, the British Parliament passed the Government of India Act 1858 (often called the 'Act for the Good Government of India'). It abolished the East India Company entirely. The powers of government, territories, and revenues were transferred directly to the British Crown. 
DECOY BUSTING: The Pitt's India Act (1784) had previously established the dual control of the Company and the Crown. The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition for civil services. The Indian Councils Act 1861 started the portfolio system.
EXAM INSIGHT: Queen Victoria's Proclamation (read out by Lord Canning at the Allahabad Durbar in Nov 1858) officially announced this change. It also promised non-intervention in religious matters and the end of annexations (killing the Doctrine of Lapse).
